Pulmonary Circulation — Quick Reference

Normal Values / Key Formulas

All values: 80-120 mmHg (systolic blood pressure), 40-80 mmHg (pulmonary artery pressure). Formulas: CO = SV x HR, SVR = (MAP - RAP) / CO.

Classification

TypeDescription
Pulmonary HypertensionPA pressure > 25 mmHg
Pulmonary EmbolismBlockage of pulmonary artery

Drug Doses

Oxygen: 2-10 L/min inhalation q1h, Nitroglycerin: 0.4-0.8 mg SL q5min. Monitoring parameters: oxygen saturation, blood pressure.

Diagnostic Criteria

  1. Pulmonary artery pressure > 25 mmHg
  2. Oxygen saturation < 90%

Mnemonics

LEFT - Low oxygen, Elevated pulmonary pressure, Fluid overload, Tachypnea. RACE - Rest, Oxygen, Analgesia, Compression, Elevation.

Exam Traps

Common mistakes: Correct answer: Pulmonary Embolism vs wrong choice: Deep Vein Thrombosis, Correct answer: Oxygen therapy vs wrong choice: Anticoagulation. Other mistakes include Correct answer: Hypoxia vs wrong choice: Hypercapnia, Correct answer: Pulmonary Hypertension vs wrong choice: Pulmonary Edema.

Quick Recall

  • 80-120 mmHg - Normal systolic blood pressure
  • 40-80 mmHg - Normal pulmonary artery pressure
  • 25 mmHg - Threshold for pulmonary hypertension
  • 90% - Threshold for oxygen saturation
  • 2-10 L/min - Oxygen therapy dose range
  • 0.4-0.8 mg - Nitroglycerin dose range
  • SVR - Systemic Vascular Resistance
  • CO - Cardiac Output
